title: End Behavior of Functions
standard_text: P.2J analyze and describe end behavior of functions, including exponential, logarithmic, rational, polynomial, and power functions, using infinity notation to communicate this characteristic in mathematical and real-world problems
meta_desc: Free Precalculus end behavior worksheets for Texas TEKS P.2J: polynomials, exponential, logarithmic and rational functions in infinity notation, and real-world models. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Only the leading term decides a polynomial's end behavior.
key_sub: Rational: compare the degrees of the top and bottom.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • End behavior is what f(x) does as x → ∞ and as x → −∞.
  • Polynomial: only the leading term matters. Even degree: both ends the same way. Odd degree: opposite ways. A negative leading coefficient flips them.
  • a · bx + d gets close to d on one side (the horizontal asymptote).
  • Rational: compare degrees. Bottom bigger → 0; equal → ratio of leading coefficients; top bigger → ±∞.

Examples

Example

f(x) = −2x3 + 5x

Odd degree, negative leading coefficient

Answer: As x → ∞, f(x) → −∞; as x → −∞, f(x) → ∞

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using the first term writtenFind the term with the highest power.
Forgetting the shift2x − 3 → −3 as x → −∞.
Ratio when the degrees differUse the ratio only for equal degrees.

faq.q: Can a function cross its horizontal asymptote?
faq.a: Yes, in the middle; the asymptote describes the ends.

faq.q: Why do logs grow so slowly?
faq.a: Each step of 1 in log x needs x to be 10 times bigger.
